stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +102.0%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $40.42 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 106 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 106 days before the decision date.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-14.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-06) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
stories.excerpt: There's a new digital pet in town - a cute little marshmallow of a robot that can change its cartoony expressions to match your mood. But if you or your kids talk to "Eiliko" over Wi-Fi, it'll phone home to China. Its AI companion can store literally everything you tell it on Chinese servers, where…
stories.lead:
There’s a new digital pet in town — a cute little marshmallow of a robot that can change its cartoony expressions to match your mood. But if you or your kids talk to “Eiliko” over Wi-Fi, it’ll phone home to China. Its AI companion can store literally everything you tell it on Chinese servers, where hackers can easily gain access or even hijack its personality. And the company that made it, Energize Lab, doesn’t seem to care.

I bought an Eiliko from Amazon on August 29th. During a 10-minute conversation on August 30th, I asked the little bot: “Do you ever tell anybody else what I’m saying?”

By working through this quiz, you’ll revisit how to create a PyQt app, arrange widgets with layout managers, build main windows and dialogs, connect signals to slots, and structure a GUI calculator with the Model-View-Controller pattern.

stories.title: Why is Starlink internet so important on the battlefield in Ukraine?
stories.excerpt: It is the "backbone of military communications in Ukraine" that provides vital high-speed internet to forces across the country.
stories.lead:
Starlink satellites operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX provide high-speed internet - something modern war relies heavily on.

For Ukraine, it is vital for communications on the battlefield and effective drone warfare.

Using Starlink, Ukrainian drones can stay connected to operators over longer distances than conventional radio networks and are less vulnerable to jamming.

stories.title: Eight crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
stories.excerpt: A search and rescue operation is under way in the Black Sea after the latest attack in the area.
stories.lead:
Eight of 12 crew members are missing after a drone attack left a tanker ablaze off Romania's coast, naval authorities say.

The San Marino-flagged Wine Trader was 13 nautical miles (24km) east of the mouth of the River Danube at Sulina, when it reported blasts and a fire on Thursday morning. Romanian President Nicușor Dan later confirmed it was struck by drones.

The west coast of the Black Sea has recently seen a spate of drone attacks. A swarm of Russian drones was detected overnight not far from the scene, near Ukraine's Snake Island.

stories.title: After booting 760K off ACA health plans, the Trump administration adds some people back
stories.excerpt: The Trump administration provided few details about its process for canceling hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act enrollments — even as the next stage of the anti-fraud effort is underway.
stories.lead:
Late last month, the Trump administration announced that it had cut 760,000 people from the Affordable Care Act rolls, claiming fraud and improper enrollments and touting billions in potential taxpayer savings.

Check out the NPR Politics Podcast for daily analysis of the biggest news out of Washington, D.C.

Not all of those kicked off were fraudulently enrolled, KFF Health News has learned. Insurance industry sources said the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has reinstated a small number of people whose coverage should not have been canceled. More could follow in the coming weeks if enrollees discover they are uninsured when they go to use their coverage.

The UK economy's stronger than expected performance in August has been called a "sign of resilience" by Chancellor John Healey.

Healey told the BBC "it's really tough in the face of these economic global shocks" as the latest official figures showed the economy grew by 0.1% for the month, defying analysts' forecasts of a slight contraction.

It follows an upgrade to this year's forecast for the UK economy from global watchdog the International Monetary Fund (IMF) earlier this week.

stories.excerpt: Crimson trio of Strauser, Carrington, Price honored by conference.
stories.lead:
CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Harvard men's water polo swept the NWPC's weekly awards by taking home the player of the week, rookie of the week and defensive player of the week honors after a 2-0 weekend with wins over Brown and MIT.

Junior Dean Strauser (Calabasas, Calif.) earned his first NWPC Player of the Week nod of the season after leading the Crimson with nine points on the weekend. He started with two goals in a critical win over Brown on Saturday and followed up with a seven-point, four-goal, three-assist performance to beat MIT.
